translation.title: Diclofenac Diethylammonium Gel
translation.efficacy: This medicine is used for pain relief and reduction of inflammation in traumatic inflammation of tendons, ligaments, muscles and joints (such as sprains and bruises), localized forms of soft-tissue rheumatism (such as tendovaginitis, shoulder-hand syndrome, bursitis and periarthritis), and localized forms of rheumatic disease (such as osteoarthrosis of the peripheral joints and spine).
translation.usage: Adults and adolescents 12 years and older: depending on the size of the painful area, apply 2 to 4 g at a time to the affected area 3 to 4 times a day and rub it in gently. Unless directed by a doctor, do not use this medicine for more than 7 days for muscle and joint injuries, and do not use it for more than 14 days in total.
translation.caution: Do not use this medicine if you are hypersensitive to it, if you have or have had hypersensitivity reactions such as asthma, angioedema, hives or acute rhinitis caused by aspirin or other nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory analgesics, for children under 12, or if you are pregnant or breastfeeding. Consult a doctor or pharmacist before use if you are elderly, if you have bronchial asthma, or if you are or have been hypersensitive to propylene glycol. This medicine is for external use on the skin only - do not swallow it. Do not use it on skin with lesions (bleeding skin disorders, eczema, infected lesions, burns or wounds), or in the eyes or on mucous membranes. If your symptoms do not improve or become worse after 7 days of use, stop use immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist. Do not breastfeed while using this medicine. Wash your hands thoroughly after use (except when applying it to finger joints). Do not use an occlusive (airtight) dressing over it. Refrain from smoking while using this medicine and keep away from open flames. If you are taking loop diuretics (such as furosemide), thiazide diuretics, medicines that interfere with blood clotting (such as warfarin), antiplatelet medicines (such as aspirin), selective serotonin reuptake inhibitors or serotonin-norepinephrine reuptake inhibitors, consult a doctor or pharmacist. Adverse reactions may occur - commonly rash, eczema, erythema (red patches) and dermatitis (including contact dermatitis) and itching, rarely blistering dermatitis, and very rarely hypersensitivity reactions (including hives), angioneurotic edema, asthma, photosensitivity reactions or pustular rash; if any of these occur, stop use immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist. If serious skin reactions such as exfoliative dermatitis, Stevens-Johnson syndrome or toxic epidermal necrolysis, or serious gastrointestinal reactions including bleeding, ulcer or perforation of the stomach or intestines occur, stop use immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist. Using it on damaged skin can cause temporary irritation and a tingling sensation, so use it with care. Store below 25 degrees Celsius and keep out of reach of children.
